verdicts.reason: Confirmed as anticipates, as a restatement. This agrees with the g1 verifier's labels for the two sources the passage cites, [27] Minic 2020 (arXiv:2003.00318) and [70] BHM 2021 (arXiv:2010.15610), and for Hübsch–Minic 2026 (arXiv:2604.19418), all anticipates. §3.2 gives each field φ_λ(x, x̃) a dual field φ̃_λ(x, x̃) that does not commute with it; integrated over the dual spacetime label, 'it is a candidate for the invisible matter sector (dual to the observed, visible, Standard Model sector)'. §5 repeats it. Unlike the review and 2202.06890 (both partial), this paper supplies the frame that makes 'dual' mean C1's mirror polarization. Spacetime 'can be viewed as a specific polarization in modular spacetime'. η is 'the polarization (or locality) metric', which separates the spacetime-like from the dual-spacetime-like aspects of phase space. ω is the canonical commutator of x and x̃, 'or ... q and p in quantum theory'. That is C1's identification in substance: each Standard Model field has a partner in the conjugate polarization, and that sector is the dark-matter candidate. The program calls χ a candidate too (#11 §12), so the hedge does not lower the label. The reader's differences are accurate. The dual fields do not commute with the visible ones ([x, x̃] = iλ²), a metastring feature that strict P4 lacks. The paper does not say that the dual sector gravitates like ours, though its source Minic 2020 does. It has no velocity gate, no monopoles and no momentum-space kinematics. It is not independent: priority for C1 is Minic 2020.
